newsitem.title: USA: D.C. delegate set to reoffer flat tax bill Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: D.C. delegate set to reoffer flat tax bill Tuesday.

text.p: Eleanor Holmes Norton, the District of Columbia's delegate to the U.S. Congress, plans to reintroduce her bill to create a 15-percent flat tax for the financially struggling city on Tuesday, her staff said.
Norton will outline the bill at a press briefing here at 1030 EST time on Capitol Hill, according to a written statement.
Norton's bill would scrap the current federal tax schedule, which has rates as high as nearly 40 percent.
It would set a federal income tax ceiling for District residents at 15 percent and cut capital gains taxes on investments by D.C. residents in the city.
D.C. residents would pay no capital gains on investments made within the District. Mortgage interest and charitable contributions deductions would continue.
Norton offered the measure originally in April 1996, but no committee action was taken.
